text: Stephanie, hypothetical question. If you could choose any city in the United States tomorrow, where would you go?
If it were only about the weather, I would choose Florida. But it is not.
The person. If my old professor were in Alaska, I would go to Alaska.
And your son? Would he go with you?
If the position lasted a year, yes. If it were three months, I would come back to him.
If I were you, I would ask for the short one first.
That is what everybody says. If the short one worked, the long one would become easier.
If I had six months free, I would spend them in a research center.
If I were not working with data, I would probably be back in surgery.
The biggest challenge would be the language, not the medicine.
What would you do if you were in my situation?

People always ask me if I would go back. Honestly, I do not know. If someone offered me a research year abroad tomorrow, I think I would say yes, but the answer is not simple. My daughter is eleven. If she were three, I would take her and she would learn the language in a month. At eleven it is different. And if I left for a year, I would lose the position I have here, because nobody keeps a job open that long. So my honest answer is this: if the offer came with six months instead of twelve, I would go tomorrow. Twelve months, I would have to think very hard.

I get this question from Brazilian doctors every month, so let me be direct. If I were starting this process today, I would do three things differently. First, I would take the English exam before anything else, because it is the slowest part and everybody leaves it for the end. Second, I would write to the researcher directly instead of writing to the department, because departments do not answer and people do. Third, I would ask for three months, not a year. A short visit is much easier to approve, and if it goes well, the second one is almost automatic. That is what I would do. What you do is your decision.
